=== Hillock David and Amy - Protest Letter Against Bell County East to Big Hill (Docket 59475).pdf ===
David & Amy Hillock
258 Fawn Ridge Dr
Copperas Cove, Texas 76522

Impacted Property Address:

133 Alta Vista Dr, Lampasas, Texas 76550
S7425 ROLLING HILLS RESERVE LOT 28, PHASE 1

Date: April 27, 2026



Subject: Motion to Intervene and Statement of Opposition

Docket No. 59475 – Bell County East to Big Hill 765kV Transmission Line (Route H5 / H42)



To the Public Utility Commission of Texas,

We, David & Amy Hillock, are property owners in Burnet County, Texas. We respectfully submit
this letter as a formal Motion to Intervene in Docket No. 59475 and to state our opposition to
proposed Routes H5 and H42 associated with the Bell County East to Big Hill 765kV
Transmission Line Project.



I. Statement of Interest

We are the owners of approximately 10.6 acres located at 133 Alta Vista Drive within the Rolling
Hills Reserve subdivision. We recently sold our home in the Dallas area to relocate to the Texas Hill
Country, where we are currently in the final design stages of constructing our permanent residence.

Our planned improvements include a custom-built home and detached workshop, representing a
significant financial investment of approximately $1.3 million. However, beyond the financial
investment, this property represents a deeply intentional lifestyle shift—one centered around
family, nature, and long-term land stewardship.

Our home was specifically designed and oriented to maximize the surrounding natural views,
particularly the southern vista of rolling hills. Proposed Route H5 directly borders our southern
property line and would significantly impact this primary viewshed. Route H42 would similarly
affect the northern view corridor at the front of our home.

These views were a primary factor in our decision to purchase this property.



II. Environmental and Land Use Impact
 Our property consists primarily of a natural pond and native juniper and mature live oak trees,
which are widely recognized as suitable habitat for the Golden-cheeked Warbler, a federally
protected species under the Endangered Species Act. While we are not asserting confirmed
occupancy, the composition of our land reflects the type of habitat that supports nesting and
breeding activity for this species within Central Texas.

In addition, our property includes a large pond that supports a diverse ecosystem of birds,
amphibians, and pollinators. Our plans include enhancing this environment through:

   •   Establishing honeybee hives to support pollination and local agriculture
   •   Planting native, pollinator-friendly vegetation
   •   Preserving and enhancing bird nesting habitats
   •   Maintaining the ecological balance of our land and water resources

The introduction of a 765kV transmission line in immediate proximity to our property would
fragment habitat, disrupt wildlife patterns, and undermine these long-term conservation efforts.



III. The "Existing Easement" Fallacy & Aesthetic Injury

We understand that portions of the land south of our property are being considered due to an
existing utility easement. However, we strongly contend that placing a 765kV transmission line
within this corridor represents a significant escalation in scale and impact. Our home is
architecturally oriented toward the south to utilize the natural topography and vistas.

Replacing these 180° natural views with 200-foot steel lattice structures constitutes a Total Loss of
Aesthetic Value for our primary living areas, destroying the "Reserve" character of the community.



IV. Economic and Community Impact

The Commission is required under PURA § 37.056 to consider community values and economic
integrity. Rolling Hills Reserve is a high-growth residential engine for Burnet County, currently
containing 111 distinct Property IDs.

We have modeled the projected revenue loss to the Lampasas ISD and Burnet County based on a
very conservative 10% annual increase in new housing starts over the next 10 years.

The "Opportunity Cost" of Segments H5/H42:

   •   Depreciated Base: Real estate data for rural residential tracts shows a 10%–15% valuation
       suppression for homes in the immediate "visual zone" of 765-kV lines.
   •   Compounded Loss: In a scenario where 5 to 6 new homes are completed annually in the
       impacted zones of Phase 2, a $75,000 "stigma discount" per home results in a taxable base
       loss of $7.5 million by 2036.
    •   Agency Deficit: At current combined tax rates, this project would result in a cumulative loss
       of approximately $410,000 in school and county revenue over the first decade alone.

By choosing segment H5 or H42, the State is effectively asking the local taxpayers of Burnet County
and the students of Lampasas ISD to subsidize this utility project through a permanent reduction in
their future tax base.

In reality, the placement of these lines would more likely cause potential, future homeowners to
avoid the area entirely, resulting in a total loss of residential growth.



V. Loss of Use, Enjoyment, and Intended Purpose

We did not relocate to Burnet County to live adjacent to industrial-scale infrastructure. We chose
this property, within a residential subdivision, to build a home that reflects a quieter, more
intentional way of living—closer to our grandchildren, closer to nature, and grounded in long-term
sustainability.

The placement of a 765kV transmission line along our property boundary would fundamentally alter
that vision and significantly diminish both the use and enjoyment of our land. Simply put, this
would place a massive blight across the very Hill Country landscape that drew us to this
property and inspired our investment and that of our neighbors.



VI. Lack of Opportunity to Participate

We closed on the purchase of our property on November 3, 2025. The change in property
ownership was recorded by the Central Appraisal District on November 7th. Even so, we have never
received any form of notification from Oncor or any other entity. Had we not been made aware by
our neighbors, we would not have known about the project, at all.



VII. Requested Relief

We respectfully request that the Commission:

   •   Reject the entire plan. Sources of local generation should be developed that service the
       areas needing greater capacity
   •   Reject proposed Routes H5, out-of-hand and H42, if possible, due to their impact on a
       residential neighborhood, environmentally sensitive land, and community development
   •   Require appropriate environmental review of affected areas, including habitat
       considerations
   •   Evaluate alternative routing options that utilize existing high-voltage corridors or less
       impactful land configurations, avoiding residential use areas, wherever possible.
 Thank you for your time and consideration of this matter. We intend to remain actively engaged
throughout this process and advocate for an outcome that respects both private property rights and
responsible land use.



Respectfully,

David and Amy Hillock
